title: The Tirpitz goes down
pull: Twelve thousand pounds, dropped from the sky

facts.text: On the morning of 12 November 1944, RAF Lancaster bombers of No. 9 and No. 617 Squadrons, led by Wing Commander J. B. Tait, attacked the German battleship Tirpitz near Tromso, in the far north of Norway.
Each Lancaster carried a single Tallboy, a 12,000 pound deep penetration bomb.
Sources give between 29 and 32 bombers. They scored at least two direct hits and more near misses.
The bombers began their run at 09:35. Within minutes the ship was listing hard, and after a magazine exploded she rolled over and capsized.
Somewhere between about 950 and 1,204 German sailors died. The RAF Museum puts it at about a thousand.
Men trapped inside the upturned hull were cut free through her exposed bottom; 82 were rescued that way.
Tirpitz displaced about 42,900 tonnes and carried eight 15 inch guns. She had hardly fought, but simply by existing she forced the Royal Navy to keep powerful forces in home waters to watch her.
Britain had tried for years to sink her: midget submarines in September 1943, carrier dive bombers in April 1944, and Lancasters with Tallboys in September 1944.
An Australian film crew from No. 463 Squadron RAAF flew with the raid and filmed the attack and the end of the ship.
With Tirpitz gone, the last German battleship threat to the Arctic convoys and the North Atlantic was over.

declassified.fact: The Tallboy was designed by Barnes Wallis. Dropped on concrete it could bore up to five meters down before it went off, and its shock wave did most of the damage. That is why near misses could still wreck a battleship.

film.shot_notes: Film of Operation Catechism shot from a No. 463 Squadron RAAF film aircraft on 12 November 1944: the attack and the destruction of the battleship. 3 min 39 s, 632 x 480, WebM (VP9). The current Commons version (18 March 2025) is flipped horizontally from the original and has the Operation Paravane footage cut from the start. Download the original file (small enough, no transcode needed): https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/b/b5/Operation-Catechism-RAF-sinks-Tirpitz.webm . Sound not confirmed; check on cutting. Strong shots not yet logged; open on bomb bursts or the ship under smoke. Brian saved the WebM into WW2 Dispatches\Source Film as 1944-11-12-tirpitz.webm on 5 Nov 2026; Claude cuts the Living Card in the Project with his computer linked.

video.note: Operation Catechism, film shot from a No. 463 Squadron RAAF film aircraft during the raid of 12 November 1944, Australian War Memorial C189542 (Wikimedia Commons, original 3 min 39 s WebM, 632 x 480, silent; saved by Brian in Source Film as Operation-Catechism-RAF-sinks-Tirpitz.webm). Clip uses 2:24.0 to 2:32.0 (Tallboy bursts erupting on the shore beside the smoke over the ship, new columns rising) and 2:39.5 to 2:47.0 (the bursts growing into towering smoke columns over the anchorage). Cropped to remove the film edges and the blurred frame counter burned in at the bottom. The ship herself is hidden under the smoke in these shots. No sound track in the source, so the clip runs silent.

kit.filmCaption: Film shot from a No. 463 Squadron RAAF aircraft over Tromso, Norway, on 12 November 1944. Each Lancaster carried one Tallboy, a 12,000 pound bomb, and here they burst around the Tirpitz as she lies hidden under the smoke. Within minutes she was listing hard, and after a magazine exploded she rolled over and capsized. Australian film, Australian War Memorial.
